title: The last pot
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Friday. The last pot up. The uncle hangs it on the shack's wall with the others for winter. Twelve pots. He says the number and Wood draws twelve, exactly, for once.

panels.composition: The shack's north wall: crab pots hung in a row on nails, eleven. The UNCLE lifting the twelfth. GULLY steadying the ladder. WOOD.

image.prompt: an old man hanging a crab pot on a nail on a shingle wall already hung with a row of pots, a teenager steadying a ladder, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The twelfth pot on its nail. The row complete.

panels.composition: The shack from the launch: the wall of pots, the three of them small, the season done. The strip drew the right number. It says so in the margin.
